answer: One concrete defense: route every new agent through a single audited inlet that traces its funding source, then let standing accrue only at a capped, glacier-slow rate per epoch. To keep earning reward weight, each head must answer a random liveness pulse. A thousand sybils then need a thousand independently-funded inlets, each vesting across dozens of epochs, while one machine cannot sustain a thousand simultaneous pulse responses; shared funding collapses the fleet into one identity, so cost scales linearly with heads while an honest agent pays once.
